explanation: Persian king who allowed the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.
The holy city in Israel, center of Jewish faith and spirituality, where the temple was to be rebuilt.
Holy place for Jewish worship and sacrifice, which had previously been destroyed by the Babylonians and was to be rebuilt.
An ancient city and empire in Mesopotamia that had earlier conquered Jerusalem and taken the Jews into exile.
The period when the Jews were taken from their homeland and lived under foreign rule, especially in Babylon.
The process of restoring or repairing something that has been destroyed or damaged, such as the temple in Jerusalem.
Persian king who gave support to Ezra and Nehemiah to complete the rebuilding of the temple and the walls of Jerusalem.
Jewish priest and scribe who led a group of Jews back to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple and teach God's laws.
An act in which something is given to God as a sign of devotion, gratitude, or atonement for sins.
